**QUESTION 2: TEXT RECONSTRUCTION (15 marks)**

*Read the following text, find the mistakes in it and correct them. Then, copy the corrected text in your answer booklet, underlining all the identified corrected mistakes.*

Adolecence is a period of great challenge particularly the young child. Around the child is a fast-changing developing world. Some of these developments are now increasing to be seen in the public domain. Since the young are separated by age difference, their language develops in different way.

I noticed this as we lived in Kumba for ten years when we moved to Douala last year. There in Kumba, we enjoyed music, especially from X-MALEYA Dance Group that are playing together for over twenty years. Leonine, one of us, will be disappointed if she'll fail her exams because of this music pass time

In our quater, there are many ideal youth at every road junction. My girlfriend and me phone us everyday to talk about the things happening there. Most often, the news from our area aren't very good. For. instance, she asked the other day if some passer-bys stopped and helped an old man who fell over and weather neighbours child hurt it when it fell out of the bed.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Corrected text** (the corrections are in bold; in the answer booklet they must be underlined)

**Adolescence** is a period of great **challenge, particularly for** the young child. Around the child is a fast-changing developing world. Some of these developments are now **increasingly seen** in the public domain. Since the young are separated by age difference, their language develops **in a different way**.

I noticed this as we **had lived** in Kumba for ten years when we moved to Douala last year. There in Kumba, we enjoyed music, especially from X-MALEYA Dance Group that **has been playing** together for over twenty years. Leonine, one of us, will be disappointed if she **fails** her exams because of this **pastime**.

In our **quarter**, there are many **idle youths** at every road junction. My girlfriend and **I** phone **each other every day** to talk about the things happening there. Most often, the news from our area **isn't** very good. For instance, she asked the other day if some **passers-by had** stopped and helped an old man who **had fallen** over and **whether a neighbour's** child **had** hurt **itself** when it **had fallen** out of the bed.

**Faults and corrections (24 items, of which no. 13 is optional)**

| # | Original | Correction | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Adolecence | Adolescence | spelling (adolescence: -sc-) |
| 2 | challenge particularly | challenge, particularly | punctuation: a comma before the participial phrase "particularly ..." |
| 3 | particularly the young child | particularly for the young child | missing preposition after "challenge ... particularly" |
| 4 | increasing to be seen | increasingly seen | adverb of degree (increasingly) + past participle, not a verb + infinitive |
| 5 | in different way | in a different way | missing article before a singular countable noun |
| 6 | we lived in Kumba for ten years when we moved | we had lived in Kumba for ten years when we moved | past perfect for an earlier past action (the ten years came before the move) |
| 7 | Dance Group that are playing | Dance Group that has been playing | subject-verb agreement (singular group) and present perfect continuous with "for over twenty years" |
| 8 | if she'll fail | if she fails | first conditional: present simple, never "will", in the if-clause |
| 9 | music pass time | this pastime | spelling: one word (pastime) |
| 10 | (no full stop after "pass time") | pastime. | punctuation: end of sentence |
| 11 | quater | quarter | spelling |
| 12 | ideal | idle | wrong word (ideal = perfect; idle = unemployed, doing nothing) |
| 13 | youth | youths | plural of "youth" after "many" (optional correction: "young people" is also accepted) |
| 14 | girlfriend and me phone | girlfriend and I phone | subject pronoun (I), not the object form (me) |
| 15 | phone us | phone each other | reciprocal pronoun for two people who phone one another |
| 16 | everyday | every day | "everyday" is an adjective; the adverbial phrase is two words |
| 17 | news ... aren't | news ... isn't | "news" is uncountable and takes a singular verb |
| 18 | passer-bys | passers-by | plural of the compound noun: the first element takes the -s |
| 19 | stopped and helped | had stopped and helped | backshift in reported speech ("asked ... if") |
| 20 | who fell over | who had fallen over | backshift in reported speech |
| 21 | weather | whether | confused homophone (weather = climate; whether introduces an indirect question) |
| 22 | neighbours child | a neighbour's child | possessive apostrophe (singular) and missing determiner |
| 23 | hurt it | had hurt itself | reflexive pronoun, and backshift (had hurt) |
| 24 | when it fell out | when it had fallen out | backshift: the fall came before the question |

**Note.** The printed text also contains a stray full stop in "For. instance"; it is simply removed ("For instance"). Other small choices of the original ("age difference", "fast-changing developing world") are acceptable English and need no change.

**How to score well.** Read the text twice: once for spelling and punctuation, once for grammar (tenses, agreement, pronouns, prepositions) and for words that are real but wrong (ideal, weather). Correct only what is wrong, copy the whole text, and underline each corrected word; a candidate who rewrites sentences that were already correct may lose marks.

**Common mistakes**

1. Missing the reported-speech backshift in the last sentence (stopped, fell, hurt) because the sentence "sounds" acceptable.
2. Correcting the spelling mistakes only and leaving the grammatical ones ("she'll fail", "are playing", "aren't").
3. Not copying the whole corrected text, or forgetting to underline the corrections.
